races.name: Peter Sunderland Cheltenham Certainty Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cappa Lass
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who showed useful Irish point form but has been off for nearly a year, making her very hard to assess
runners_data.comment: Point runner-up who makes rules debut with Harry Cobden booked; betting may be informative
runners_data.spotlight: 8l runner-up in Irish mares' maiden point (3m, good to yielding) last April on second start and sold for 30,000euros in May; this half-sister to useful 2m hurdle winner Cottesloe Sunshine has Harry Cobden booked for her rules debut, for which she wears a hood; the betting may be informative.

runners_data.name: Diamond Grace
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful O'Neill yard who was backed on debut despite poor show, suggesting improvement expected
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in her sole bumper and she may be one for further down the line
runners_data.spotlight: Backed into 11-1 from 18-1 when soundly beaten fifth of eight on debut in bumper at Warwick (2m, soft) in February; this half-sister to Scottish National winner Macdermott may be one for further down the line.

runners_data.name: First Candidate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has been consistent runner-up twice recently and represents the in-form Skelton team
runners_data.comment: Point winner; runner-up in big field on handicap debut at Kelso and has leading claims
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner who is 0-4 over hurdles but has run well to finish second on last two starts (2m, soft/good to soft), most recently in a big-field handicap at Kelso; leading claims for last year's winning yard.

runners_data.name: Dolly Drama
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with encouraging bumper form who should appreciate the step up in trip on this better ground
runners_data.comment: Made the frame in both bumpers and she could have an each-way chance on hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Encouraging third on debut in Wetherby bumper (2m, soft) in November and similar form when fourth of seven at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) last month; this half-sister to the stable's smart performer Minella Drama is open to improvement and could have an each-way chance on hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Atlantic City
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who sets the standard with multiple hurdle placings but hasn't won in 9 attempts
runners_data.comment: 0-9 in Ireland but has shown ability and makes British debut with new trainer in fine form
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 in Ireland for Ciaran Murphy and unraced since last October, but she's finished third over hurdles on four occasions (2m-2m4f, various ground), showing a fair level of ability in the process; makes her British debut with her new trainer in fine form and could be involved.

runners_data.name: Flash Bardot
runners_data.note: Hold-up type switching from flat racing after poor recent form, making stable debut for new connections
runners_data.comment: Useful on the Flat in 2024 but form went wrong way last year; changed hands for 10,000gns
runners_data.spotlight: Useful on the Flat for Jack Channon up to autumn 2024; however, her form went the wrong way last year and she was sold for 10,000gns in December; needs to turn things around on this hurdle/stable debut

runners_data.name: Rose Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who was tailed off badly on both recent hurdle starts and looks completely outclassed here
runners_data.comment: Very modest on the Flat nowadays and tailed off last month on her first two hurdle starts
runners_data.spotlight: Very modest on the Flat nowadays and tailed off last month on her first two hurdle starts; a transformation is needed.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer making hurdle debut after 846 days off and showed nothing in modest flat company
runners_data.comment: 0-9 on the Flat and achieved very little; makes hurdle/stable debut after a long absence
runners_data.spotlight: 0-9 on the Flat for Lisa Williamson and achieved very little; makes hurdle/stable debut after a long absence and she would be a shock winner.

races.paceDynamic: Atlantic City will take this field along at a sustainable pace from the front, with no genuine speed horses to pressure her early. The prominent runners Diamond Grace and possibly Dolly Drama will sit handy, while the majority including First Candidate, Flash Bardot, Rose Light and Pink Walls will settle towards the back in typical hold-up fashion. With a moderate gallop likely and no fierce early tempo, this setup strongly favours patient hold-up horses who can produce their best effort late in the piece.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Atlantic City sets only a modest pace and the field comes to them late
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows held-up runners to conserve energy and unleash their finish. First Candidate and Flash Bardot can time their challenges perfectly when the tempo lifts approaching the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Atlantic City gets soft fractions and sees off late challengers
scenarios.body: Her previous consistent third-place efforts suggest she stays well, and if unopposed early she can tough it out. The hold-up brigade leave their runs too late on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Diamond Grace or Dolly Drama sit perfectly in behind Atlantic City
scenarios.body: They get the ideal trip tracking the leader without doing the donkey work early. When Atlantic City weakens, they inherit the lead with the hold-up horses still too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders all disappoint and an outsider emerges
scenarios.body: Cappa Lass shows her Irish point form was genuine or Flash Bardot's flat speed translates immediately. The pace collapses and allows a complete shock to unfold.

watchPoints.text: Atlantic City could get uncontested fractions if no other horse wants to go forward early and become very hard to peg back
First Candidate has been running well in defeat lately but needs to prove she can get her head in front when it matters
Diamond Grace was backed on debut despite running poorly, suggesting connections expect significant improvement second time out
Flash Bardot represents Henrietta Knight returning to training but the mare's recent flat form was abysmal
Cappa Lass hasn't been seen for nearly a year since her Irish point success, making her fitness a major unknown

races.name: Pertemps Network Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Final Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dance And Glance
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with improved form this season, 56 days off could be ideal freshening up, good going suits
runners_data.comment: Improved form this term and can be excused latest run in the gruelling William Hill Hurdle
runners_data.spotlight: 6yo who has shown improved form this season, winning at Ascot (1m7f, soft) in December then runner-up at Sandown (2m, good); well-beaten fifth in the gruelling William Hill Hurdle at Newbury (2m, heavy) in February; has had a break since and could play a leading role if back to his best.

runners_data.name: Williethebuilder
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with recent winning form, needs luck from back but has the class, 7lb claimer reduces weight burden
runners_data.comment: Improved this winter; soft ground may not have suited at Cheltenham; might not be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row at Kempton (2m, good) in the winter before another good run when fourth at Musselburgh (1m7f, good to soft), where he would have been a bit closer but for late interference; soft ground may not have been ideal in the County Hurdle three weeks ago; might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Smart Decision
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the pace scenario, good course and distance winner, recent poor form concerning
runners_data.comment: Went close over C&D in January; possible excuses on last two starts; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Won four of his five starts in 2025 and went close off 1lb higher than today over C&D (good to soft) in January; below par on last two starts but the 2m5f trip then soft ground are possible excuses; no surprise if he bounces back with a good performance in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: We're Red And Blue
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who can win from the lead, good recent form but will face pace pressure
runners_data.comment: Good form continued when third in the Imperial Cup at Sandown and he holds solid claims
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Huntingdon (2m, soft) in December and has continued in good form, finishing second to Williethebuilder at Kempton (2m, good) then third of 18 in the Imperial Cup at Sandown (2m, soft); solid claims.

runners_data.name: Castelfort
runners_data.comment: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Non-runner.

runners_data.name: Ice In The Veins
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won when making the running, contradictory evidence but hold-up style preferred
runners_data.comment: Pulled hard when no threat in first two handicaps; could yet be capable of much better
runners_data.spotlight: Made the running when winning two novice hurdles in November (2m3f/2m, good); ridden with restraint and pulled hard when failing to threaten in February in his first two handicaps (2m, good to soft/soft); could yet be capable of considerably better for his top yard, and a return to more prominent tactics might be the catalyst for an improved performance.

runners_data.name: Tashan
runners_data.note: Front-runner with settling issues, long absence since December, headgear applied but attitude questions remain
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 4yo who could be suited by the big-field scenario; retains potential
runners_data.spotlight: Despite failing to settle he showed a good attitude to win a 4yo handicap at Exeter (2m, good to soft) in November; pulled up at Ascot in December but that was his first run on soft going and he bled from the nose; very lightly raced and could be suited by the big-field scenario; retains potential.

runners_data.name: Frontier Prince
runners_data.note: Prominent racer needing to find extra form, tongue-tie applied, good going record but confidence lacking
runners_data.comment: Needs to better his winter form but perhaps this 5yo will be aided by the tongue-tie
runners_data.spotlight: He needs to find something extra on his last three performances but this novice hurdle winner (good to soft) is now 2lb lower than when third of 15 on handicap debut at Cheltenham (2m, soft) in November, and perhaps he'll be aided by the first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Mr McLoughlan
runners_data.note: Hold-up novice with solid autumn form, strong recent third suggests readiness for handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Third behind two unexposed rivals at Stratford; strong pace should see him to good effect
runners_data.spotlight: Novice who won three times in the autumn (2m, good to soft/good) and ran well when third behind two unexposed rivals at Stratford (2m, soft) last month; a strong pace seems likely, which should see him to good effect.

runners_data.name: Bucephalus
runners_data.note: Veteran front-runner with course form, bounced back well last time, will set strong pace but stamina tested
runners_data.comment: Career-high mark but has run really well (including over C&D) on two of last three starts
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who was second over C&D (good) in December and bounced back from being pulled up in the William Hill Hurdle at Newbury (heavy) to make all in four-runner handicap at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft); has a career-high mark in this hotter race but he did it comfortably last time; could make a bold bid.

runners_data.name: Inedit d'Amour
runners_data.note: Prominent racer struggling since easy maiden win, blinkers applied but form trend concerning
runners_data.comment: Easily won maiden hurdle at Catterick in January but soundly beaten in two handicaps since
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French 5yo who won a maiden hurdle easily at Catterick (1m7f, good) on New Year's Day on his third British start; however, soundly beaten in two handicaps since (2m3f/2m1f, good to soft) and others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Marche d'Aligre
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from wind surgery, step forward last time but needs to confirm progress
runners_data.comment: Step back in right direction at Newbury in February but very much needs to build on it
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up twice in a row at the end of last year (2m, soft) then tailed off at Ascot (2m3f, soft); following wind surgery he took a step back in the right direction at Newbury (2m, good to soft) in February but was still soundly beaten, and very much needs to build on that latest effort.

races.paceDynamic: Bucephalus, We're Red And Blue, and Tashan will ensure a strong gallop from the start, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. The middle section will see fierce congestion as Smart Decision, Dance And Glance, Frontier Prince, Marche d'Aligre, and Inedit d'Amour all want prominent positions, creating traffic problems approaching the final two hurdles. The genuine pace and stamina demands of this 1m7½f trip will stretch the field, with the hold-up horses Williethebuilder, Ice In The Veins, and Mr McLoughlan needing luck in running to get clear shots. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can secure good positions early and avoid the mid-race scramble, while making life difficult for hold-up horses who need the race to fall apart.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go too hard early and weaken approaching the last
scenarios.body: Smart Decision or Dance And Glance can track the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle, then strike when the leaders falter. Their prominent style avoids traffic while benefiting from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters can dictate terms without burning out
scenarios.body: Bucephalus has the class to make all if allowed to control the tempo, while We're Red And Blue showed he can win from the front at Huntingdon. The others may race too keenly trying to match them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Hero Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and gaps appear late for the closers
scenarios.body: Williethebuilder has winning form at this level and can finish strongly if getting a clear run, while Ice In The Veins won twice by making ground late. They need luck but have the class to capitalise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Compromised Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go steady and it becomes a tactical affair
scenarios.body: Mr McLoughlan could benefit from his hold-up style in a slowly-run race where his finishing kick matters more. Tashan might also improve for the easier pace after his settling issues.

watchPoints.text: Bucephalus and We're Red And Blue will likely dispute the early lead and could burn each other out in a speed duel
Smart Decision sits perfectly to benefit if tracking the pace but his recent poor form suggests confidence issues
Williethebuilder has the class to win but needs significant luck in running from his hold-up position
Tashan's settling problems could be exacerbated by the strong early pace, making him hard to ride
The prominent contingent of five horses could create serious traffic problems turning for home

races.name: Pertemps Network Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Final Handicap Hurdle (Series Final) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Jakar Du Moulin
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with wind surgery completed, proven on good ground with back-to-back wins including over 3m at Doncaster
runners_data.comment: Handicapping last three starts, on last two winning at Ascot and Doncaster; latter by 7l
runners_data.spotlight: Given wind surgery before handicapping on last three starts, on last two winning at Ascot (2m7f) in December and Doncaster (3m, again good to soft; from I Am Max) three weeks ago; the latter was by 7l from the front, since which he's been handed an 8lb rise but this 7yo retains potential.

runners_data.name: Super Survivor
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist in excellent form this winter, won narrowly over C&D in December but needs pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: C&D win in December; battled back for a clearcut win at Warwick (3m2f) on latest outing
runners_data.spotlight: Back in good form this winter, including on last two starts (good to soft) when he prevailed narrowly over C&D in December and battled back for a clearcut win at Warwick (3m2f; from Porter In the Park) four weeks ago; raised another 4lb but the return to a sharper test is more of a worry.

runners_data.name: I Am Max
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who was short-headed here previously, finished second to Jakar Du Moulin at Doncaster so form ties up well
runners_data.comment: Second to Jakar Du Moulin when returned to hurdling at Doncaster (3m); stable in good form
runners_data.spotlight: Short-headed on his only start here; won a Hexham chase in October; hasn't done as well since, finishing runner-up to Jakar Du Moulin when returned to hurdling at Doncaster (3m) on latest start but he needs to build on that markedly; stable in good form.

runners_data.name: Blue Carpet
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making good progress over hurdles, won stylishly at Wetherby last time and suited by step up in trip
runners_data.comment: Raised 7lb but it's easy to think he has significantly more to give after his Wetherby win
runners_data.spotlight: Made a solid start to hurdling career on good ground; second on handicap debut at Newbury in November and went one better next time in taking fashion at Wetherby (again about 3m on soft) in February; raised 7lb but it's easy to think he has significantly more to give.

runners_data.name: Porter In The Park
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner who excels under Cameron Johnstone-Baker's 7lb claim, strong recent placings form
runners_data.comment: Never better when placed under Cameron Johnstone-Baker last three runs; needs a bit extra
runners_data.spotlight: Never better than when placed under Cameron Johnstone-Baker at Ascot (2m7f), Kempton (3m, again on good) and Warwick (3m2f, good to soft; behind Super Survivor) on last three outings; a bit extra is needed to win this warm race.

runners_data.name: Ernest Gray
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning to cheekpieces, 105 days since last run could be a concern but has course-winning form
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back; a return to form looks possible for in-form yard; place hopes
runners_data.spotlight: Did well in cheekpieces last year, winning at Worcester (2m7f, good) in May and Aintree (3m, good) in October; not so good behind Super Survivor here (good to soft) in December but a return to form today looks possible for in-form yard; place hopes.

runners_data.name: Heather Honey
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with excellent course record (4W5P from 15 runs), won here over 3m in December showing she handles track
runners_data.comment: Raised another 6lb and in grade after a convincing C&D win but she's progressing well
runners_data.spotlight: Won three in a row last April-June (about 2m7f, good) and resumed her progress with convincing wins at Catterick (3m1f, good) in November and Haydock (3m, good to soft) one month ago; raised another 6lb and in grade but such a progressive mare cannot be dismissed.

runners_data.name: Secret Trix
runners_data.note: Defending champion racing off 1lb lower mark, fitted with cheekpieces and tongue-strap suggesting connections expect improvement
runners_data.comment: Won this race in 2024; 1lb lower mark today; back in some form latest; wind surgery since
runners_data.spotlight: 6-26 over hurdles, including a win with first-time cheekpieces in this race in 2024 (soft) and he is 1lb lower today; ridden by 7lb claimer last four outings, with a big return to some form on latest (second at Market Rasen) and that has been followed by his second wind operation; cheekpieces (absent on last four starts) return; too well handicapped to be ignored.

runners_data.name: Walden
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with good recent form, won quality Ascot handicap seven weeks ago but Tom Lacey's 0/6 recent record is concerning
runners_data.comment: 2-3 in handicaps; stylish when taking 18-runner race at Ascot (2m7f, good to soft) latest
runners_data.spotlight: Won a good-ground maiden last April and two of his three handicaps this winter; latest was in 18-runner race at Ascot (2m7f, good to soft) seven weeks ago in which he travelled well and asserted on the run-in to score by just over 6l; 8lb higher today but more in the tank; major player.

races.paceDynamic: Ernest Gray will be the primary pace-setter with Porter In The Park, Jakar Du Moulin, and I Am Max settling prominently behind him in the early stages. With only one confirmed front runner in a 9-horse field over 3m½f, Ernest Gray can dictate a sustainable gallop without pressure, allowing the race to develop into a tactical affair. The lack of pace pressure means the prominent runners can track comfortably while the hold-up horses (Super Survivor, Blue Carpet, Heather Honey, Secret Trix, Walden) will need the leaders to come back to them in the final stages. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit handy to the pace and have something left for a sustained drive from 3f out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactical Win
scenarios.trigger: If Ernest Gray sets a steady gallop and the pace doesn't quicken until late.
scenarios.body: The prominent runners can sit comfortably in behind before launching sustained challenges from 3f out, with the hold-up horses struggling to make up ground on the better ground. Jakar Du Moulin and I Am Max are perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes messy or Ernest Gray goes too slowly through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: The lack of genuine pace allows the back-markers to creep closer than usual, setting up a sprint finish where class and finishing kick become crucial. Super Survivor and Blue Carpet have the highest official ratings to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Ernest Gray gets an easy lead and his stamina reserves prove superior.
scenarios.body: The combination of an uncontested lead and good ground conditions allows Ernest Gray to build a decisive advantage turning for home, with his proven course form counting heavily. His October Aintree win on good ground over 3m shows he can sustain a gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the final mile creating a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure test of finishing speed rather than stamina, allowing a horse with tactical speed like Secret Trix or Walden to emerge from the pack. This scenario requires the leaders to stop dramatically.

watchPoints.text: Ernest Gray's 105-day absence could see him rusty early or fade late despite his natural front-running style
Super Survivor needs genuine pace to be effective and may struggle if Ernest Gray sets a pedestrian gallop
Secret Trix's tongue-strap and cheekpieces combination suggests breathing or focus issues that need monitoring
Cameron Johnstone-Baker's 7lb claim gives Porter In The Park a significant weight advantage over the main dangers
Jakar Du Moulin and I Am Max finished 1st and 2nd at Doncaster so their form clash provides a key reference point

races.name: Unibet Middle Distance Veterans' Handicap Chase (Series Final)

runners_data.name: Courtland
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from 113-day break under the Bowens, needs the run but effective fresh
runners_data.comment: Ran well in defeat in the main last year but minimal movement in his mark and this is warm
runners_data.spotlight: He ran well in defeat in the main last year and is effective when fresh; could give a good account on this first start since December but there's been minimal movement in his mark this season and he may again prove vulnerable in this competitive contest.

runners_data.name: Numitor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has pulled up twice this season, concerning recent form trend
runners_data.comment: Step back in right direction at Exeter and could take another today; won this race in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in this race last year and same outcome on first two runs this season; 13l fourth behind Genois at Exeter (2m3f, good to soft) last month following wind surgery and a break but he could improve for that outing, and he won this race in 2024; not written off.

runners_data.name: Le Milos
runners_data.note: Prominent runner from powerful Skelton yard but inconsistent this season, wears cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in Stayers' Veterans' Final in January but soundly beaten at Warwick since
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the Stayers' Veterans' Final at Sandown (3m, good) in January two starts ago and he's not ruled out today; however, he's been inconsistent this season and was soundly beaten at Warwick (2m4f, heavy) in February; he may prefer a longer trip than this nowadays; fourth in this last year.

runners_data.name: Triple Trade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two wins this season, strong recent Cheltenham third behind younger horses
runners_data.comment: Two wins this season and last two defeats came against younger rivals in tough handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins this season (2m/2m4f, soft/good) and 10l third behind an 8yo and a 7yo at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) in January; 20l fourth in another competitive handicap at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) in February but that form is working out well and he's back against fellow veterans today; chance.

runners_data.name: Outlaw Peter
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning to form, wears first-time cheekpieces for Nicholls team
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with 1l second to Genois at Exeter and he's on the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off favourite at Exeter (2m3f, good to soft) four weeks ago and returned to form with 1l second to Genois, finishing clear of the remainder; wears first-time cheekpieces and he's on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Guard Your Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who made all at Warwick, brought down last time but proven at this level
runners_data.comment: Won easily at Warwick in February and brought down at first fence at Cheltenham last month
runners_data.spotlight: Brought down at the first fence in the Plate at Cheltenham last month; made most of the running when winning easily at Warwick (2m4f, heavy) in February and, although now 8lb higher, he was rated higher over hurdles earlier in his career; versatile ground-wise; one to note.

runners_data.name: Dubai Days
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who specializes in spring months, won at Ayr 40 days ago
runners_data.comment: This is his time of year and he won at Ayr 40 days ago; runner-up in this race in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: His last six wins have come in the months of February, March or April and he returned to form to win at Ayr (2m4f, soft) 40 days ago; runner-up in this race two years ago (soft) and won over C&D (good to soft) last February; that latest win reads well and a 4lb rise isn't harsh; possible player.

runners_data.name: Neon Moon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who hasn't kicked on since November Ascot win, wears tongue tie and blinkers
runners_data.comment: Won in a small field at Ascot in November but has failed to kick on subsequently
runners_data.spotlight: He won a four-runner handicap at Ascot (2m5f, good) in November but has failed to kick on subsequently, proving no match for Genois and Outlaw Peter when fifth at Exeter (2m3f, good to soft) four weeks ago.

runners_data.name: Fugitif
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse winless since December 2023, wears cheekpieces and visor for first time
runners_data.comment: Best of the rest behind easy winner Guard Your Dreams at Warwick; mark continues to fall
runners_data.spotlight: Winless since December 2023 and hasn't posed a serious threat this season; however, he was best of the rest behind easy winner Guard Your Dreams at Warwick (2m4f, heavy) last time and continues to drop down the weights; handles various ground; not ruled out in first-time visor (replacing cheekpieces).

runners_data.name: Minella Drama
runners_data.note: Lone pace setter who ran well behind Protektorat last time, now 5lb lower in weights
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent nowadays but has dropped to a handy mark and he ran well last time
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent nowadays but ran well in second when facing an impossible mission behind Protektorat at Kelso (2m7f, good to soft) last time; now 5lb lower than when third in the Old Roan Chase at Aintree (2m4f, good to soft) in October and this C&D winner is capable of being involved.

runners_data.name: The Flier Begley
runners_data.note: Prominent runner defending his crown, fresh from 11-day break after recent pulled up effort
runners_data.comment: Won this last year; ran okay in recent novice hurdle; could build on it now back chasing
runners_data.spotlight: Won this last year (good) and followed up at Market Rasen (2m5f, good) in June off a mark 1lb higher than today's; pulled up/tailed off over fences on next two starts but his recent outing over hurdles was fairly encouraging and he could build on that now back chasing.

runners_data.name: The Widdow Maker
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 145-day break, good recent form but needs career best
runners_data.comment: 17l sixth in this last year; in good form on both outings this season but needs extra
runners_data.spotlight: Won in a small field at Exeter (2m3f, good) last March before 17l sixth in this race (good); he's run well in defeat on both starts this season but needs something extra if he's to come out on top today.

runners_data.name: Whistleinthedark
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who performs best fresh after breaks, returning from 113 days off
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent but his last two wins have come off the back of similar breaks to this one
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent last year but won twice (3m/2m4f, good/soft), those victories coming on the back of respective breaks of 89 and 120 days; may be best caught fresh nowadays so is worth a second look after 113 days off.

runners_data.name: Filanderer
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who failed to settle over longer trip at Cheltenham, back to preferred distance
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in the Ultima at Cheltenham but highly progressive previously; could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up in the Ultima at Cheltenham last month but that was his first attempt at a staying trip and he failed to settle out wide; went to the Festival having won five of his previous six starts (2m3f-2m5f, various ground) and he could bounce back with a big effort now back down in trip and grade.

runners_data.name: Genois
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in excellent form with recent Exeter win, proven distance specialist
runners_data.comment: Rejuvenated 10yo who has won two of his last three and is firmly in calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wetherby (2m3f, soft) on Boxing Day before good second there (2m3f, soft) in January, and he returned to winning ways at Exeter (2m3f, good to soft) four weeks ago when clear with Outlaw Tom; this rejuvenated 10yo still has mileage in his mark and is firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Lord Baddesley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who jumped left at right-handed Ascot, Haydock's left-handed track suits better
runners_data.comment: Some good runs this season and heavy ground excuses latest effort; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won three-runner handicap at Newbury (2m4f, good) on reappearance; jumped left when 6l third of four at right-handed Ascot (2m5f, good) next time, and his 13l sixth of nine at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) came in a race that worked out extremely well; heavy going excuses him being tailed off at Warwick and he could go well now back on better ground.

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: Hold-up Irish challenger with solid Killarney form, beaten soundly in recent starts
runners_data.comment: Irish challenger who is one to watch in the betting, but soundly beaten on last three runs
runners_data.spotlight: Irish challenger who could be in the picture judged on his good form at Killarney last summer, and he's one to watch in the betting; however, he's been soundly beaten on his last three starts and has to get back on track.

races.paceDynamic: Minella Drama will set the pace unopposed early as the only confirmed front runner, creating a sustainable gallop that won't trouble the hold-up horses. The real tactical battle unfolds behind him where seven runners (Numitor, Le Milos, Outlaw Peter, Guard Your Dreams, Neon Moon, The Flier Begley, The Widdow Maker) all want prominent positions, guaranteeing traffic problems and interference 2-3 fences out. With good ground conditions maintaining stamina demands over 2m4f and likely bunching at the business end, this setup creates a perfect storm for hold-up horses who can avoid the mid-race scramble and finish strongly past tired prominent runners. The race shape heavily favours hold-up performers who can pick their way through traffic late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners clash for position turning for home and create interference
scenarios.body: The pace collapses as prominent runners tire from fighting each other, allowing patient hold-up horses to sweep past with clear runs. Clean jumpers from the back division capitalize on superior finishing kick over this stamina-sapping distance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runner survives chaos
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can secure an uncontested position behind Minella Drama
scenarios.body: Guard Your Dreams or Outlaw Peter avoids the traffic, travels smoothly throughout and has enough left to resist late challengers. The winner emerges from those who positioned themselves perfectly behind the pace setter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Minella Drama leads throughout
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely with no serious challenge to the leader
scenarios.body: The front runner maintains his advantage as prominent runners cancel each other out in traffic, holding off tired pursuers up the run-in. His sustainable early pace becomes the winning tactic when others fail to organize behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Minella Drama stops or falls and no other pace angle emerges
scenarios.body: The race becomes a tactical crawl with no genuine pace, turning into a sprint finish where any running style can win depending on final furlong positioning. Chaos theory takes over with unpredictable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Traffic chaos developing 2-3 out as seven prominent runners (Numitor, Le Milos, Outlaw Peter, Guard Your Dreams, Neon Moon, The Flier Begley, The Widdow Maker) converge for position
Minella Drama's jumping under pressure if challenged turning for home, hasn't won for over a year
Guard Your Dreams and rider's 5lb claim in this competitive field after recent Cheltenham fall
Whistleinthedark and Lord Baddesley both returning from long breaks, market support indicates readiness
Triple Trade's stamina reserves in finish, two wins this season suggest peak form maintained

races.name: JCB Fastrac Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Heads Or Harps
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the expected pace scenario, strong recent form at Ayr with 29 days freshness ideal
runners_data.comment: 2m Ayr win last spring and second there three times this term, including at around 2m4f
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season with a 13l win at Ayr (2m, soft) and has finished second there on three of his five outings this term, including over an extended 2m4f the last twice; ought to be competitive again.

runners_data.name: Imperial Bede
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with first-time cheekpieces adding urgency, though 41-day break may need the run
runners_data.comment: Catterick win in February; poor run since but good shout if putting best foot forward
runners_data.spotlight: Evidently not the force of old but he built on an encouraging C&D reappearance when winning in first-time cheekpieces at Catterick (2m3f, soft) in February; made early mistakes when a disappointing favourite at Hereford since but it's possible he'll be happier back on a left-handed course and likely he's still on a winnable mark if putting his best foot forward.

runners_data.name: Count Adhemar
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfect for tracking the leaders, improving fence form and well-weighted at 157lbs
runners_data.comment: Good second in 2m handicaps in recent months; won't need to improve much for longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 6yo; improved form since switched to fences, finishing second in 2m handicaps at Ludlow (soft) and Newcastle (good to soft) in recent months; the return to a longer trip won't need to unlock much improvement.

runners_data.name: Victoria Milano
runners_data.note: Front runner returning from 59-day break with first-time tongue-tie, but fall last time out is concerning
runners_data.comment: Well held in two hurdles runs for new yard and well beaten in previous outing over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Well handicapped on some of her old hurdle form for Alastair Ralph but she looked held when falling in a 2m5f handicap hurdle here on her reappearance in January; down the field at Ludlow since and hard to know what to expect back chasing (well beaten on previous attempt).

runners_data.name: Bonza Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent Exeter win, cheekpieces retained and proven at this trip
runners_data.comment: Another Exeter win in January and just as good when second at Wincanton since; a player
runners_data.spotlight: Added to his strong chase record at Exeter with a win over the extended 2m1f there (good to soft) in January; just as good when runner-up over 2m4f on heavy at Wincanton since; bold show likely off the same mark.

runners_data.name: I Shut That d'Or
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 390 days off, previous hat-trick form gives him chances fresh
runners_data.comment: Three wins last winter but off since stopping quickly at Stratford 390 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: His form took off with three wins over fences last winter; however, his good run came to an abrupt halt at Stratford last March and he hasn't been seen since; no great record fresh to date but the betting is perhaps the best guide to his chance.

runners_data.name: Royal Deeside
runners_data.note: Second front runner with recent course experience, 3lb claimer takes useful weight off
runners_data.comment: Two Hexham wins this season; back in form when third latest but isn't the most consistent
runners_data.spotlight: Successful twice over 2m4f at Hexham (good) this season; bounced back from a couple of poor runs when third of 13 at Carlisle (2m4f, good to soft) 13 days ago but his rather in-and-out record of late suggests he's no good thing to back that up.

races.paceDynamic: Victoria Milano and Royal Deeside will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front runners likely to set a solid gallop over this extended 2m4f trip. Count Adhemar, Bonza Boy and I Shut That d'Or will track the pace prominently, while hold-up horses Heads Or Harps and Imperial Bede will be held back for late strikes. The dual pace setters should ensure an honest tempo that will stretch the field, though neither looks strong enough to dominate throughout. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers and hold-up horses who can benefit from the strong gallop and kick late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders go too fast early and weaken approaching the final fence
scenarios.body: The honest gallop will set up perfectly for the back-markers to sweep past tired leaders. Heads Or Harps and Imperial Bede have the class and tactical pace to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Count Adhemar or Bonza Boy can sit just behind the leaders and time their challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows the prominent runners to stay close enough to pounce when the leaders weaken. Their positioning gives them first run on the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Deeside can dictate from the front and see off Victoria Milano's challenge
scenarios.body: The 6-year-old's recent Hexham wins show he can dominate from the front over this trip. His class edge allows him to repel late challenges on good ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long Absence Success
scenarios.trigger: If I Shut That d'Or returns fresh from his 390-day break and benefits from the strong pace
scenarios.body: His previous hat-trick shows his ability when right, and the long rest could have him primed for a bold comeback. The pace will suit his prominent style perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Victoria Milano could set unsustainable fractions if she battles too hard with Royal Deeside early
Imperial Bede needs to be produced with perfect timing from his hold-up position after the 41-day break
I Shut That d'Or's market support will reveal connections' confidence after his lengthy absence
Count Adhemar must not get caught behind the two leaders if they go too slow early
Heads Or Harps requires Derek Fox to keep him interested throughout the race from his hold-up position

races.name: JCB Hydrogen Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Lawtan
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with French form over similar trips, 21 days since last run should have him spot-on for this longer distance test.
runners_data.comment: Stayed on strongly for 4yo chase win in France over 2m3f; not discounted on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Stayed on strongly to win a 4yo chase in France (2m3f, good to firm) last October; 33-1 when 14l fifth on stable debut in novice hurdle at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) three weeks ago; the step up in trip may be a plus on this first handicap start and he's not discounted.

runners_data.name: Largy Go
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from top yard but trainer running at just 3% strike rate over past 14 days, needs pace to collapse late.
runners_data.comment: Point winner who was placed on first two hurdle starts and could relish this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won sole Irish point last March (3m, yielding to soft), after which he was sold for £305,000; placed on his first two hurdle starts (2m, heavy/soft) this year; his dam's wins came over 2m7f/3m and he could relish this step up in trip on handicap debut; has obvious potential off opening mark.

runners_data.name: Kadjar Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Prominent racer switching back to hurdles after chase experience, good record at this distance range on softer ground.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up off this mark over fences in February; not ruled out now back over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of promise in novice hurdles (including on good to soft) and runner-up over fences in handicap at Doncaster (3m, soft) in February; reverts to hurdles having unseated over fences last month; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Kenzo Des Bruyeres
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with proven stamina from Irish point wins, wears cheekpieces and 34 days off could leave him vulnerable late.
runners_data.comment: Two-time point winner; soundly beaten on both hurdle starts but may be capable of better
runners_data.spotlight: Easily won two Irish points (3m, good to yielding/soft) last autumn; soundly beaten when fourth at Ffos Las (2m4f, heavy) on his two hurdle starts but he may yet be capable of better; makes handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Mighty Fleur
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who hasn't won over hurdles, 79 days since last run is a significant concern for fitness.
runners_data.comment: Has shown promise but needs to bounce back from two lesser shows (chase debut last time)
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in two bumpers and three novice hurdles; disappointing in novice hurdle at Uttoxeter in December and well beaten on chase/handicap debut at Newcastle in January; return to form needed now back hurdling.

runners_data.name: Brookside La
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from in-form Skelton yard, shaped like this longer trip would suit when third here in January over 2m5f.
runners_data.comment: Kept on well over 2m5f here in January and this longer trip could suit
runners_data.spotlight: Won on handicap debut at Wetherby (2m3f, soft) on Boxing Day before 4l third of 17 here (2m5f, good to soft) in January, when shaping as though this longer trip could suit; in excellent hands to continue to progress.

runners_data.name: Springtime Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who made all at Hereford but usually comes from behind, wears hood and has solid recent form.
runners_data.comment: Won at Hereford in February and good third at Wincanton since; might not be far away
runners_data.spotlight: Made all with something to spare at Hereford (2m5f, heavy) in February on second handicap start and another good run when third at Wincanton (3m, good to soft) last month; might not be far away.

runners_data.name: Times Are Green
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with just one good run from four starts, early faller last time adds to reliability concerns.
runners_data.comment: Early faller when 18-1 on handicap debut; yard is in excellent form; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Just the one good run in his three novice hurdles but that was when 11l second at Chepstow (2m7f, good to soft) in December; early faller when 18-1 for recent handicap debut at Newbury (3m, good to soft); his stable is in excellent form and he could run well in first-time cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Big Storm Brewing
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with back-to-back wins on softer ground, climbing weights but clearly progressive and suited by 3m trips.
runners_data.comment: Up in the weights but clearly progressive having won his last two; unexposed at the trip
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the tenth attempt, at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) last month, and followed up at Musselburgh (3m, good to soft); climbing the weights but clearly progressive and unexposed over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Kenzo Des Bruyeres is the only confirmed front runner and will set a steady, uncontested pace from the start in this 9-runner field over 3m½f. With Lawtan, Kadjar Des Mottes and Mighty Fleur likely to settle prominently behind him, there's enough early pace to create a genuine test but not enough speed to create a collapse scenario. The large contingent of hold-up horses (Largy Go, Brookside La, Springtime Legend, Times Are Green, Big Storm Brewing) will be relying on the leaders maintaining their gallop to the business end. This sustained but manageable pace clearly favours the prominent racers who can track the tempo and strike when it matters most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders maintain a strong gallop to 2 out and the hold-up horses struggle to make ground.
scenarios.body: Lawtan and Kadjar Des Mottes are perfectly positioned to capitalize as Kenzo Des Bruyeres weakens, with their class and tactical positioning proving decisive. The hold-up brigade find too much to do as the race doesn't fall apart late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres goes too fast early or the pace collapses after halfway.
scenarios.body: Big Storm Brewing and Springtime Legend get the perfect setup as the early leaders fade dramatically in the final half-mile. Their superior finishing kicks overwhelm tired leaders who went too hard too soon.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Kenzo Des Bruyeres gets an easy lead and kicks clear turning for home.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes pedestrian early, allowing Kenzo Des Bruyeres to conserve energy before producing a sustained drive that the field cannot match. His two Irish point wins over 3m suggest he has the stamina to make all pay.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes messy with multiple horses vying for position throughout.
scenarios.body: Times Are Green or another unconsidered runner benefits from a muddling pace that doesn't suit the obvious contenders. The tactical battle between multiple prominent runners creates gaps for a horse with different tactics.

watchPoints.text: Kenzo Des Bruyeres could go too fast early if challenged by the prominent runners, as he's been keen in previous starts.
Mighty Fleur's 79-day absence combined with disappointing recent form makes him unreliable despite his prominent running style.
Big Storm Brewing faces a 7lb rise for his recent wins and may find this company significantly stronger than his previous victories.
Largy Go represents the powerful O'Neill team but their poor recent strike rate suggests timing issues with their runners.
Times Are Green's early fall last time means fitness is unknown and his reliability remains questionable.

races.name: JCB Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Laganhill
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who stays well, first-time cheekpieces added and 43 days since last run could freshen him up
runners_data.comment: Second of four at Exeter six weeks ago; in the mix again off an unchanged mark
runners_data.spotlight: Dual soft-ground hurdle winner at around 2m; has looked a thorough stayer over fences, 4l second of four over 3m at Exeter (heavy; first-time cheekpieces) six weeks ago; in the mix again off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Cerendipity
runners_data.note: Prominent runner well-treated on best form, but struggling recently and jumping issues are a concern
runners_data.comment: 9lb lower than for last win but has been struggling; cheekpieces off, tongue-strap on
runners_data.spotlight: Well treated on his best form, now 9lb lower than when winning at Newcastle (2m7f, good to soft) in March 2025, but he has been struggling, including with his jumping; cheekpieces off, tongue-strap on.

runners_data.name: Ski Lodge
runners_data.note: Proven at course and distance with solid Haydock record, cheekpieces back on after disappointing Wetherby effort
runners_data.comment: Bit disappointing last time but cheekpieces and a return to Haydock could see a revival
runners_data.spotlight: Has a win and a second (over C&D) from two runs here; bit disappointing at Wetherby five weeks ago after looking dangerous early in the straight, but cheekpieces and a return to Haydock could see a revival.

runners_data.name: Jacks Parrot
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form including good Tommy Whittle fourth, ideal for strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Fourth over C&D in December and creditable runs since; however, more required to win
runners_data.spotlight: Creditable fourth in the Tommy Whittle over C&D (soft) just before Christmas and has run to a similar level both starts since; no obvious reason why he won't be thereabouts again but he'll need something extra to win.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Des Bordes
runners_data.note: Out-and-out stayer who won at Warwick, Charlie Maggs 3lb claim helps but was below par last time
runners_data.comment: Ran well over 3m4f here in December but well below par last time and others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Looks an out-and-out stayer; ground out victory at Warwick (3m, soft) in December and ran well over 3m4f here next time, but he was well below par on latest start and others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Buckna
runners_data.note: Non-runner, had won twice at Hereford but recent form poor
runners_data.comment: Two wins late in 2025 but poor since and needs to be revived by cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins over 3m1f at Hereford late in 2025 but has run poorly on both outings since and needs to be revived by cheekpieces.

runners_data.name: Saladins Son
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner, most likely pace-setter with solid course form and 49 days freshening break
runners_data.comment: Running well this term, including over C&D; hard to knock and should be thereabouts again
runners_data.spotlight: Most consistent since chasing debut, twice making the frame over C&D (good to soft/soft) and again running creditably when a close third of six at Wincanton (3m1f, heavy); hard to knock and should be thereabouts again.

runners_data.name: One Last Glance
runners_data.note: Leading rival who seems better than ever at nine, Freddie Mitchell 3lb claim valuable at bottom weight
runners_data.comment: Arrives in form after win and good second at Leicester; receives lots of weight all round
runners_data.spotlight: Seems better than ever at the age of nine and he followed a 2m4f win at Leicester (heavy) with a good second there over 2m6f (good to soft); stays at least 3m and he receives lots of weight all round; respected.

runners_data.name: Fortunedefortunata
runners_data.note: Form has fallen off badly since leaving Gordon Elliott, needs major revival under new trainer Patrick Morris
runners_data.comment: Badly out of form in the last 12 months and needs to be revitalised by a change of stables
runners_data.spotlight: Mostly campaigned in competitive handicap chases when with Gordon Elliott, and his form has fallen off a cliff; changed hands for £3,000 in February; needs to be revitalised by a switch of stables.

runners_data.name: Major Fortune
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form for Dan Skelton, perfectly positioned for strong pace over this trip
runners_data.comment: Prolific hurdles winner, just as good over fences; second at Leicester latest; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner over hurdles; just as good over fences and holding his form well, beaten off only on run-in when second at Leicester (2m6f; stays 3m1f well) four weeks ago; handles any ground; leading contender.

runners_data.name: Solar System
runners_data.note: Encouraging fence debut suggests improvement to come, hold-up style suits if building on Southwell third
runners_data.comment: 4-14 over hurdles; pleasing start over fences and solid claims if building on that run
runners_data.spotlight: Four wins (2m1f-2m5f) over hurdles; made an encouraging start over fences when 3l third of six at Southwell (3m, soft) last month; solid claims if building on that run with cheekpieces now fitted.

runners_data.name: If Not For Dylan
runners_data.note: Veteran who won making all at Doncaster but faces stronger opposition and 6lb rise
runners_data.comment: Veteran who retains enthusiasm; jumped well and made all at Doncaster; back up 6lb
runners_data.spotlight: Veteran who retains enthusiasm, and he jumped well and made all at Doncaster (3m, good to soft) in February, but he's back up 6lb and probably in a stronger race here.

runners_data.name: My Bobby Dazzler
runners_data.note: Won positively at Hereford but up 5lb and may need similar tactics from Toby McCain-Mitchell
runners_data.comment: Put everything together when winning at Hereford; up 5lb and in a stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Put everything together when winning at Hereford (3m1f, soft) six weeks ago under a positive ride from Toby McCain-Mitchell; not discounted but he's up 5lb and this is a stronger race.

races.paceDynamic: Saladins Son and One Last Glance are confirmed front-runners who will engage early, with Saladins Son the more consistent pace-setter likely to take them along. The presence of two keen leaders should create an honest gallop over this stamina-sapping 3m1½f trip at Haydock, with the pace likely to be solid throughout rather than stop-start. Several prominent racers like Laganhill, Ski Lodge and Cerendipity will track the leaders closely, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Major Fortune, Solar System and Jacks Parrot will look to pounce late. This strong early pace over a staying trip clearly favours the hold-up merchants who can conserve energy and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners duel early and set a solid gallop
scenarios.body: The strong pace will set up perfectly for the patient types to come with late runs, particularly those with proven stamina. Major Fortune, Solar System and Jacks Parrot are ideally positioned to benefit from this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers can get the perfect trip behind the leaders
scenarios.body: Horses like Ski Lodge or Laganhill could steal a march by avoiding the early duel but staying close enough to strike. They get the best of both worlds with a decent position and some pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners disappoint or one backs out of the early contest
scenarios.body: A slower pace would disadvantage the hold-up horses and potentially favour those who can press on from mid-race. The prominent racers would be best placed to capitalize on a muddling pace scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Saladins Son or One Last Glance gets loose on the front end
scenarios.body: One of the leaders could steal a march if the other fails to engage, allowing for controlled fractions and a strong kick for home. Saladins Son's consistency gives him the edge in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Saladins Son and One Last Glance engaging in early speed duel could set this up perfectly for hold-up horses
Ski Lodge jumping at Wetherby last time - needs to regain his fluent style to utilize course and distance advantage
Solar System building on encouraging fence debut - any market confidence would be significant given trainer form
Major Fortune getting prominent early position despite hold-up style - Harry Skelton may press forward if pace moderate
Jupiter Des Bordes and stamina test - this trip should suit but needs to bounce back from below-par Haydock effort
